title: Trig value of a radian angle using the unit circle
subtitle: Circles · 5 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **5 of the official questions in Circles are this one** — 1 Easy, 1 Medium, 3 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question asks for sin, cos or tan of a radian angle.
- The angle is often larger than 2π, or built from another angle by multiplying it.
- The choices are special values like ±1/2, ±√2/2, ±√3/2, ±√3 or ±1.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Build the angle if it is defined through another one.
- Then subtract multiples of 2π (a full turn) until it is between 0 and 2π.
- 2) Find its reference angle and quadrant.
- 3) Use the unit-circle point (cos, sin) to get the value with the right sign.
- For tangent, divide y by x.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Desmos works in radians by default, so type the trig function of the angle exactly as written and compare the decimal with the choices worked out as decimals.
Check that the degree setting is off.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You get the size right but the sign wrong because you misjudged the quadrant after reducing the angle.
Or you use a sine value where the question asks for cosine.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
